'''Andrew Marc Weiner''' [[OSA Fellow|OSA]] [[National Academy of Engineering|NAE]] [[National Academy of Inventors|NAI]] (Born July 25, 1958 – 2024) was an American electrical engineer, educator and researcher known for contributions to the fields of ultrafast optics and optical signal processing. He was the Scifres Family Distinguished Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at [[Purdue University]].

== Career ==
Weiner received a Sc.D. in [[electrical engineering]] in 1984 from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://link.galegroup.com/apps/doc/K3099153603/BIC?sid=lms|title=Andrew Marc Weiner|website=link.galegroup.com|access-date=2019-08-05}}</ref> Following graduation he joined [[Bellcore]], then a premier telecommunications research and development company, eventually serving as Manager of Ultrafast Optics and Optical Signal Processing Research. In 1992, Weiner was appointed at professor rank at the School of Electrical and Computer Engineering at [[Purdue University]].

Weiner's research in ultrafast optics focuses on the processing of extremely high-speed lightwave signals as well as their application to the generation and manipulation of ultrabroadband radio-frequency signals. He is most well-known for research on the development of Fourier synthesis methods for controlling the shape of femtosecond light pulses.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Weiner|first1=A. M.|last2=Heritage|first2=J. P.|last3=Kirschner|first3=E. M.|date=1988-08-01|title=High-resolution femtosecond pulse shaping|journal=Journal of the Optical Society of America B|volume=5|issue=8|page=1563|doi=10.1364/JOSAB.5.001563|bibcode=1988JOSAB...5.1563W |issn=0740-3224}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Weiner|first=A. M.|date=2000-05-02|title=Femtosecond pulse shaping using spatial light modulators|journal=Review of Scientific Instruments|volume=71|issue=5|pages=1929–1960|doi=10.1063/1.1150614|bibcode=2000RScI...71.1929W |issn=0034-6748}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Weiner|first1=A. M.|last2=Leaird|first2=D. E.|last3=Patel|first3=J. S.|last4=Wullert|first4=J. Findings from Weiner's research have been applied in fiber optic networks and in ultrafast optical science laboratories around the world. == Awards and honors ==
In 2008, Weiner was elected to the U.S. [[National Academy of Engineering]], "for contributions to the development of femtosecond optical-pulse shaping technology."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nae.edu/30746/Dr-Andrew-M-Weiner|title=Dr. Andrew M. Weiner|website=NAE Website|access-date=2019-08-05}}</ref> He is a Fellow of the National Academy of Inventors (2016),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.purdue.edu/newsroom/releases/2016/Q4/purdue-professor-weiner-elected-fellow-of-national-academy-of-inventors.html|title=Purdue professor Weiner elected fellow of National Academy of Inventors|last=Service|first=Purdue News|website=www.purdue.edu|access-date=2019-08-05}}</ref> the Optical Society of America (1990)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/100/osa_stories/andrew_weiner/|title=Andrew Weiner {{!}} The Optical Society|last=|first=|date=2019-08-05|website=}}</ref> and the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) (1995).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://services27.ieee.org/fellowsdirectory/getdetailprofile.html?custNum=DL0qd5zrzI6eyBQwsk7X8A%3D%3D&bccaptions=Alphabetical%20Listing%20&bclocations=%2Ffellowsdirectory%2Fhome.html|title=IEEE Fellows Directory - Member Profile|last=|first=|date=|website=[[IEEE]]|access-date=2019-08-05}}</ref> He received a National Security Science and Engineering Fellowship, now called the [[Vannevar Bush]] Faculty Fellowship,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basicresearch.defense.gov/Programs/Vannevar-Bush-Faculty-Fellowship/|title=Vannevar Bush Faculty Fellowship|website=United States Department of Defense|access-date=2019-08-05}}</ref> from the U.S. Department of Defense in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.uns.purdue.edu/x/2009a/090504WeinerAward.html|title=ECE professor awarded grant for Department of Defense research|website=news.uns.purdue.edu|access-date=2019-08-05}}</ref> He has received the Optical Society of America's Adolph Lomb Medal (1990) in recognition of his early career achievements,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/adolphlomb/|title=Adolph Lomb Medal - The Optical Society of America|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=2019-08-05}}</ref> the [[International Commission for Optics]] Prize (1997),<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://e-ico.org/node/106|title=ICO Prize {{!}} International Commission for Optics|website=e-ico.org|access-date=2019-08-05}}</ref> the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]] Research Award for Senior U.S. Scientists (2000),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://engineering.purdue.edu/Engr/People/Awards/All/ptRecipientListing|title=Alexander von Humboldt Honors - Our People - Purdue Engineering|website=College of Engineering - Purdue University|access-date=2019-08-05}}</ref> the IEEE Photonics Society's Quantum Electronics Award (2011),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.photonicssociety.org/awards/quantum-electronics-award/quantum-electronics-award-award-winners|title=Quantum Electronics Award Award Winners - IEEE Photonics Society|website=www.photonicssociety.org|access-date=2019-08-05}}</ref> and Optica's Charles Hard Townes Medal (2023).<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 Charles Hard Townes Medal Winner {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/get_involved/awards_and_honors/awards/2023_award_winner_pressreleases/2023townesmedalwinner/ |access-date=2024-08-12 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref> Weiner is the co-recipient (with Jonathan Heritage) of both the Optical Society of America's [[R. W. Wood Prize]] (2008)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/rwwood/|title=R. W. Wood Prize {{!}} The Optical Society of America|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=2019-08-05}}</ref> and the IEEE Photonics Society's William Streifer Scientific Achievement Award (1999).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.photonicssociety.org/awards/william-streifer-scientific-achievement-award/william-streifer-scientific-achievement-award-winners|title=William Streifer Scientific Achievement Award Winners - IEEE Photonics Society|website=www.photonicssociety.org|access-date=2019-08-05}}</ref> He was also recognized by [[Popular Science]] Magazine for one of the "Top 100 Inventions of 1988" for the 100-femtosecond all-optical switch.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qP9fvo9OLIwC|title=Popular Science|date=1988-12-01|publisher=Bonnier Corporation}}</ref>

Weiner has received numerous awards from Purdue University. He was awarded the Herbert Newby McCoy Award (2013),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.purdue.edu/research/awards/herbert-newby-mccoy-award/past-recipients.php|title=Past Recipients - Office of the Executive Vice President for Research and Partnerships|website=www.purdue.edu|access-date=2019-08-05}}</ref> which is the most prestigious award given by the university in natural sciences.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.purdue.edu/research/awards/herbert-newby-mccoy-award/|title=The Herbert Newby McCoy Award - Office of the Executive Vice President for Research and Partnerships|website=www.purdue.edu|access-date=2019-08-05}}</ref> He is also the inaugural recipient of the College of Engineering's Research Award (2003).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://engineering.purdue.edu/Engr/People/Awards/Institutional/Faculty/2003/ptIndexYear|title=Our People - Purdue Engineering|website=College of Engineering - Purdue University|access-date=2019-08-05}}</ref> In recognition of his mentorship, Weiner received the Purdue University Provost's Award for Outstanding Graduate Mentor (2008)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.purdue.edu/gradschool/awards/recipients-and-nominees.html|title=Recipients and Nominees - The Graduate School - Purdue University|website=www.purdue.edu|access-date=2019-08-05}}</ref> and the College of Engineering Mentorship Award (2014).

Weiner was a Hertz Fellow at MIT<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hertzfoundation.org/fellows/fellow-profile/10147/Andrew-M-Weiner|title=Andrew M. Weiner|website=hertzfoundation.org|access-date=2019-08-05}}</ref> and a recipient of the [[Hertz Foundation]] Doctoral Thesis Prize.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hertzfoundation.org/awards/thesis-winners/|title=Thesis Prize Winners|website=hertzfoundation.org|access-date=2019-08-05}}</ref>

In addition to his technical interests, Weiner has had a lifelong interest in martial arts, and holds black belt rank in Aikido and Judo.
